In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the average current trajectory preceding spike initiation is a multiphasic, dynamic wave form that is the most probable and preferred stimulus.

spike triggering by transmembrane currents is a probabilistic process in which the average current trajectory preceding the spike is the most probable value and that the current slope and acceleration are crucial for the last 200 ms before the spike.
spike initiation is a probabilistic process in which the most probable current trajectory is that which is close to the average trajectory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spike‐evoking transmembrane current was multiphasic, with the early phase opposing the bias and the late phase favouring it; that the average current trajectory was the most probable one and was the best predictor of spike triggering; that the late phase of this trajectory was most critical; and that the slope of this phase was the most effective stimulus component.

spike initiation by a transmembrane depolarizing current is a complex process involving a multiphasic trajectory of the average current, a Gaussian probability density of current values, and a high degree of correlation between current pairs.
spike initiation by transmembran current in Aplysian neurones is a highly reliable process that involves a wide variety of wave forms, but that a preferred current trajectory is involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spike initiation is a highly reliable phenomenon, that the average current trajectory preceding the spike is multiphasic and that the late phase of this trajectory is crucial in spike triggering.
spike initiation by transmembranous current is not restricted to a single type of wave form.
spike triggering is not a simple process, but rather one involving complex interactions between the transmembranal current trajectory and the cell's intrinsic properties.
